Description: Four independent bodies, each offset with solid.offset in both directions - the first regression case for that tool. Ids 1-3: a plain 40x30x20 block, grown by 3 and shrunk by 3; every edge is convex, nothing splits, and both results can be computed exactly. Ids 4-7: a cylinder r=20, h=60 with a transverse bore r=15 through its middle at z=30. Beside the bore only two crescent shaped webs of 5 mm thickness connect the upper half to the lower one, so shrinking by 4 has to consume them and break the body into TWO separate solids. Ids 8-14: a staircase built from three overlapping boxes - a prism over an 8-corner profile with 22 convex and 2 concave (reflex) vertical edges - offset in both directions, so one shape exercises both: growing rounds the 22 convex edges and trims at the 2 reflex ones, shrinking does exactly the opposite. Ids 15-19: a 40 mm cube with a 20 mm corner octant cut out, offset in both directions. Its vertices are the point of the case: at (40,20,20), (20,40,20) and (20,20,40) one concave and two convex edges meet, while (20,20,20) joins three concave edges - the vertex where GetOffset has to decide whether a spherical patch belongs there (it needs three arcs) or not.
Expected:
SIMPLE BLOCK (ids 2, 3), both exact. blockGrown is the Minkowski sum of the block with a ball of radius 3: V = a*b*c + A*r + pi*(a+b+c)*r^2 + 4/3*pi*r^3 = 24000 + 15600 + 810*pi + 36*pi = 42257.787385, A = 5200 + 576*pi = 7009.557368, extent -3,-3,-3 .. 43,33,23, surfaces PlaneSurface:6 CylindricalSurface:12 SphericalSurface:8 - one quarter cylinder per edge, one octant sphere per corner. blockShrunk is simply the block 34x24x14 at (3,3,3): V = 11424, A = 3256, extent 3,3,3 .. 37,27,17, surfaces PlaneSurface:6 and nothing else, because shrinking rounds concave edges and this body has none.
PIERCED CYLINDER (id 7). The webs beside the bore are 5 mm thick, so their largest inscribed sphere has radius 2.5: an offset of -4 removes them completely and the result must be TWO solids ('solids': '2'). The two parts are mirror images of each other in the plane z=30, so their volumes and areas must be equal to each other - that is the strongest check here, since the volume of the pierced cylinder itself (two perpendicular cylinders of different radii) is not elementary. Each part is bounded by its flat end at z=56 resp. z=4, by the outer cylinder shrunk to r=16 and by the bore grown to r=19; the offset bore therefore reaches OUTSIDE the offset outer surface (19 > 16), which is why nothing is left near z=30. Extents follow from that: the upper part runs from z = 30 + sqrt(19^2-16^2) = 30 + sqrt(105) = 40.246951 to 56, the lower one from 4 to 19.753049, both within x,y = -16..16. Both parts closed and consistent.
STAIRCASE (ids 13, 14). The profile in the x-z plane is (0,0) (30,0) (30,10) (20,10) (20,20) (10,20) (10,30) (0,30), area 600, perimeter 120, extruded 20 in y: stairs has V = 12000 and A = 3600. stairsShrunk is exact, because a prism shrinks to the eroded profile times the shortened height. The eroded profile is the staircase moved in by 2 with its two reflex corners rounded to quarter circles of radius 2 - and the rounding ADDS material there rather than removing it: the sharp inner corner of the moved-in profile lies at distance 2*sqrt(2) from the original corner, so it survives the erosion, and what the arc cuts away is only the square minus the quarter disc. Area 376 + 2*(4-pi) = 384 - 2*pi = 377.716815, perimeter 104 - 2*(4-pi) = 102.283185, height 20-4 = 16. So V = 6144 - 32*pi = 6043.469035 and A = 2304 + 28*pi = 2391.964594, surfaces PlaneSurface:10 CylindricalSurface:2 - one quarter cylinder along each reflex edge and no sphere anywhere, since no vertex joins three concave edges. stairsGrown has no comparably simple volume (the reflex edges spoil the Steiner formula), but its topology is fixed: PlaneSurface:10 CylindricalSurface:22 SphericalSurface:12 - a fillet on each of the 22 convex edges, and a spherical patch only at the 12 vertices where three convex edges meet. The four vertices at the ends of the two reflex edges carry just two convex arcs and must NOT get a sphere; their two fillets have to meet each other.
CORNER NOTCH (ids 18, 19). notched = 40^3 - 20^3 = 56000, A = 9600, 9 planar faces, 18 convex and 3 concave edges. notchShrunk is exact as well - the erosion of the 7/8 cube by a ball of radius 2 is the cube [2,38]^3 minus the corner octant dilated by 2: V = 46656 - (7776 + 166*pi/3) = 38880 - 166*pi/3 = 38706.165207, A = 7560 + 53*pi = 7726.504376, surfaces PlaneSurface:9 CylindricalSurface:3 SphericalSurface:1 - one fillet along each concave edge and exactly one spherical octant at (20,20,20), where three concave edges meet. notchGrown has no closed form here. The obvious estimate - the grown 40 cube 83200 + 1472*pi/3 minus the part of the notch that stays further than 2 from the body, taken as {x,y,z > 22}, which gives 75424 + 1306*pi/3 = 76791.64 - is about 95 too high: outside the cube the dilation does not follow those flat planes, it curves around the notch edge, so the excluded set is larger than {x,y,z > 22} there. It must read PlaneSurface:9 CylindricalSurface:18 SphericalSurface:10: the seven surviving cube corners plus (40,40,20), (40,20,40) and (20,40,40) have three convex edges each and get a sphere, while (40,20,20), (20,40,20) and (20,20,40) have only two convex edges next to their concave one and must not get one.
All ten verified results must be closed and consistent; a false in either field is a defect regardless of the measured values.
Status: PASSES (2026-09-09, commit a3f5c3ee 'Fixed some bugs with Shell.GetOffset'). Keep as a regression guard for solid.offset. The case was written before the tool worked and found two defects on its first run: growing a body with concave edges either threw or produced nothing at all. Both are fixed - the first by reversing the face orientation for a positive offset (BooleanOperation.SetFaces(faces, reverseOrientation) plus the new Operation.connectMultipleReversed), the second by guarding the null vector cases in Geometry.DistLL and Curves, which the parallel edges of the staircase ran into.
Actual: All 19 calls succeed, the fingerprint is identical over four repeats, and every result is closed and consistent. Where a closed form exists the recorded numbers match it: exactly for the bodies without curved faces (blockShrunk, stairs, notched, and stairsShrunk to 1e-9), and 5e-5 to 1e-4 above it for the bodies with fillets and spherical corners. That residue is the triangulation, not the geometry: measured at meshes from size/1000 down to size/100000, blockGrown moves -9.2e-4, +5.3e-5, +2.0e-5, +5.7e-6, +2.5e-6 and stairsGrown -1.0e-3, +1.0e-4, +3.9e-5, +1.1e-5, +5.9e-6 - a monotone walk onto the exact value, while the bodies made of planes and cylinders alone do not move at all. The metric meshes at size/4000, which is where the recorded values sit.
